requirement:
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.

Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.

Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
rationale:
structural: Structural obligations in `requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`: (1) the current set is read from SQLite; (2) one coherent database snapshot is used per check; (3) there is no historical-run search or separate report-selection metadata cache; (4) identities, states and provenance can be read without loading measurements. The remaining clauses (only complete, available results contribute; pending, running and unavailable entries are reported; no building or executing; no restoring a superseded attempt) describe observable behavior that other requirements govern.

Each structural clause is implemented in the supplied roots:
- `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#impl[Store]/fn[read]` opens `DATABASE` with rusqlite in read-only mode, which covers the SQLite obligation. It also rejects an unsupported schema version.
- `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#impl[Store]/fn[snapshot]` does the whole read inside one `connection.transaction()`. That covers the state row, the invocations, the tests, and the measurements, so a concurrent replacement cannot mix results. A reader that reads state and tests in separate autocommit queries would break the clause, which makes this transaction a real structural choice.
- The same function queries only the current `tests` rows and the `state.latest` invocation, so it does not search historical runs. It uses no separate selection cache.
- Its `measurements: bool` parameter selects `NULL` instead of the `measurements` column for metadata-only reads, so metadata is readable without loading measurements.

The saved check path is `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#fn[load_saved]`. It calls `Store::read` once and `snapshot(true)` once, so each check uses a single snapshot. That caller needs no marker because the roots carry the obligations. I did not review the other clauses against any further roots.

behavioral: I judged the tests adequate for `requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. I did not request implementation source. The reviewed tests cover each obligation, as follows.

- **One coherent snapshot.** `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[replacement_between_snapshot_queries_cannot_mix_configurations_or_results]` commits a replacement while a reader's snapshot read is in progress. It asserts that the reader sees only the old configuration, run, test identity and measurements (value 7). It then asserts that the next snapshot sees only the new set (value 9). `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[metadata_queries_skip_measurements_and_snapshots_survive_subsequent_replacement]` checks that an existing snapshot survives a later replacement.
- **Current set only, no history or metadata cache.**
  - `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[latest_started_retry_replaces_success_and_cannot_be_overwritten_by_old_conversion]` and `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[focused_replacement_preserves_unselected_results_and_shared_artifacts]` show that the snapshot holds one current entry per test, with no accumulated attempts.
  - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_corrupt_optional_metadata_cache_does_not_hide_saved_measurements]` corrupts a `selection-cache.json` file. It asserts that the store stays valid and the measurements are still used.
- **Metadata read without measurements.** The `metadata_queries_skip_measurements…` test corrupts the measurements column. `snapshot(false)` still returns identities and configuration, with `measurements` equal to `None`.
- **Only complete, available, fresh results contribute.**
  - `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[running_and_unreadable_entries_suppress_totals_even_alongside_fresh_measurements]` covers a missing profile and the pending and running states. Each is reported, the check fails, and no totals appear.
  - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]` covers failed and interrupted attempts that lack measurements, and stale results after a source change.
- **Never restores a superseded attempt.**
  - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unreadable_history_cannot_reintroduce_an_older_success]` runs four cases: invalid metadata, missing source, unsupported schema and a missing profile. In each, the newest attempt is unreadable and the older success is not restored.
  - The retry test shows that an old conversion cannot overwrite a newer attempt, and that the replaced attempt's measurements are gone.
- **No build or test execution.** `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` runs `coverage-check` with a `cargo` shim and an execution sentinel. It asserts that no test ran, that only `cargo metadata` was called, and that the stored files are unchanged.

The cited requirements `requirements.test-coverage.storage.current`, `requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness` and `requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement` are context only. I found no unmarked or missing scenarios.

text: :::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.
Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.
Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
:::{req} storage.current
The coverage set contains at most one current entry for each pair of nextest
binary identity and test name, within one active instrumented build
configuration under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`.
An entry represents either a test awaiting execution or its current attempt.
Replacing an entry removes its previous measurements from the current set.
Metadata and files shared by remaining current entries stay available. The
store does not accumulate completed historical runs or retry attempts.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.
A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
:::{req} check.measurement
The coverage check fails when the current store is missing, unreadable, or
corrupt, when no usable coverage has been collected, or when a current entry
is pending, running, missing measurements, unreadable, or stale.
Test execution outcome and measurement availability are distinct. A failed
or interrupted attempt can supply coverage if its measurement processing
completed successfully and its measurements are available. Such an outcome
does not by itself turn its measurements into zero execution or make them
unavailable.
For a current result, every referenced raw profile must remain readable and
nonempty, and matching captured source must remain available. Loss of these
artifacts makes that result's measurements unavailable.
These measurement failures are distinguished from measured lines with zero
execution and from individual functions absent from otherwise usable coverage.
Exception evidence does not excuse measurement failures or permit substitution
of a superseded attempt.
An unsupported store format, or measurements lacking the function attribution
required by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, is rejected
with guidance to recollect coverage. Missing or corrupt metadata that prevents
establishing the current test set, states, provenance, or active configuration
causes failure rather than silently checking the remaining readable records.
